summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with advanced multiple myeloma on carfilzomib, recent listeria meningitis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted with fever, headache, and cough. Imaging revealed multifocal pneumonia, prompting IV antibiotics with cefepime after initial broad coverage. He developed a drug rash likely from ampicillin, which was continued for listeria coverage with symptomatic treatment. His kidney function worsened, consistent with acute tubular necrosis, possibly from prior gentamicin or cancer therapies, but improved during the stay. He experienced delirium attributed to cefepime, which resolved after dose reduction. A lumbar puncture and MRI showed no new central nervous system infection or acute stroke. He stabilized, completed his pneumonia antibiotic course, and was discharged to rehab to finish his six-week ampicillin regimen, with adjustments to insulin and beta-blocker therapy.
